evidence: r-binding §7: Pin is load-bearing; `Host:` kept ; r-binding §7: A changed second answer is never used ; r-binding §7: Explicit, default and non-default ports ; test-fetch.R: the pin is load-bearing and Host is kept ; test-fetch.R: a changed second resolver answer is never used ; test-fetch.R: the pin holds on explicit, default and non-default ports ; test-fetch-tls.R: an IPv6 address is pinned, bracketed, with Host kept
note: reclassified: L-partial -> enforced-by-library, pinning is mandatory and wholly in-library (INV-5, INV-6), through connect_to rather than CURLOPT_RESOLVE, which fails open (r-binding.md §4.1)

external_id: OWASP Top 10:2021 A10: DNS rebinding and TOCTOU
requirement: Document the DNS rebinding and TOCTOU risk and state which mechanism closes it.
evidence: r-binding §7: One resolution per hop ; r-binding §7: A changed second answer is never used ; test-resolve.R: a name is resolved exactly once per hop ; test-fetch.R: a changed second resolver answer is never used ; test-binding.R: a name is resolved once per hop, and never again by the fetch
note: the mechanism is INV-5 (resolve once, pin); the residual is a compromised resolver (§11.2)

external_id: Available protections: Domain name (disclosure to external DNS resolvers)

external_id: Available protections: Domain name, action 1 (internal DNS server first)
requirement: Let the caller supply the resolver, so internal domains resolve through an internal resolver first.
note: reclassified: L-partial -> enforced-by-application, INV-5 forbids a public resolver argument; resolver order is the host's system configuration, which ssrfr uses as is (S5)

external_id: OWASP Top 10:2021 A10 (TOCTOU)
requirement: Do not cache resolution results across evaluations by default; any cache is caller-controlled and off by default.
evidence: r-binding §7: One resolution per hop ; r-binding §7: Every handle carries the pin; TLS never weakened; §5 "never set" options absent ; test-resolve.R: a name is resolved exactly once per hop ; test-transport.R: every handle carries the pin; TLS is never weakened ; test-fetch-limits.R: a connection is never reused, within a pin or across pins
note: corrected: no cache exists and none is configurable; each prepare resolves afresh (§2.5) and transport DNS caching cannot serve a later request (§14)

requirement: Treat a resolution failure as deny, never allow.
evidence: verdict:dns-answer ; r-binding §7: Empty answer or resolver error refuses as `unresolvable` ; test-dependencies.R: a failing parser wrapper refuses as parse, never an error ; test-dependencies.R: a failing raddr wrapper refuses as malformed-address ; test-resolve.R: an empty answer or a resolver error is unresolvable ; test-resolve.R: a failing raddr wrapper refuses an answer as malformed-address ; test-binding.R: a refusal opens no connection, whatever refused it ; test-fetch.R: a failing transport wrapper fails closed, never an R error
note: reported as the operational cause `unresolvable`, not a policy refusal (§6.2, §6.6); ASVS 5.0 V16.5.3 (fail securely) is the closer mapping, SC-7(5) being a boundary control

external_id: Available protections: Domain name (malicious payload to internal DNS resolvers)
